facts.raw_span: A man in his 80s was brought to the emergency department after a cardiac arrest
the patient was last seen healthy by his family 4 hours earlier
then was found unresponsive and pulseless in the bathroom
He underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, receiving 4 doses of epinephrine intravenously and endotracheal tube intubation with return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 10 minutes
Family later revealed he had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had been complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
A family member witnessed him struggling for air before losing consciousness
Initial rhythm was pulseless electrical activity
Sinus rhythm at approximately 100 beats per minute
Right axis deviation
Prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1
No acute occlusions found
QT interval of 360 ms measurable in leads V4-V6

support_spans: Family later revealed he had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and had been complaining of shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation
A family member witnessed him struggling for air before losing consciousness
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of shortness of breath and struggling for air, combined with the absence of acute coronary occlusions, suggest a possible pulmonary embolism.

support_spans: Right axis deviation
Prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1
concepts.why: The patient's ECG findings, including right axis deviation and prolonged QRS duration, are consistent with Brugada syndrome.

support_spans: QT interval of 360 ms measurable in leads V4-V6
concepts.why: The patient's prolonged QT interval is consistent with long QT syndrome.

The ECG findings of right axis deviation, prolonged QRS duration with rsR' complexes in lead V1, and wide S waves in leads I and V6 are consistent with right ventricular hypertrophy, which could be a contributing factor to the patient's cardiac arrest, and the absence of acute occlusions found in coronary angiography supports this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of COPD and shortness of breath for 2 days prior to presentation, along with a family member witnessing the patient struggling for air before losing consciousness, decided it.
